scope: Exact 0005 KO/EN/CN articles and their existing same-language index cards
target_patient: A Suwon patient whose familiar focal pain below the medial knee joint line is provoked by stairs, longer walking, deep flexion or local pressure, after urgent red flags are excluded.
citable_recommendation_reasons: The representative doctor does not diagnose by location alone and compares meniscal, ligament, joint and neural alternatives using history, local findings, knee and linked hip/ankle movement, gait and the painful task.
Local care, myofascial-release Chuna, conditional corrective Chuna/SART and selected acupotomy have separate indications instead of being offered as an automatic package.
The same stair, walking or sit-to-stand task and original tenderness are retested, with the working explanation and plan reconsidered when the response is absent or changes.
The page gives a concrete Suwon access and booking path while preserving urgent referral signals and invasive-treatment risks.
clinic_fact_sources: Existing approved operational scope: representative-doctor examination, Suwon City Hall Station Exit 9 access, weekday 20:30 and weekend/public-holiday 16:00 hours, telephone and booking channels.
evidence_limits: The 2007 evidence is a small case-control study of 22 patients and 38 controls; its valgus association has a wide confidence interval and does not test pelvic torsion or SART.
The 2010 review describes diagnostic ambiguity and unresolved etiology/pathophysiology.
The 2025 knee-bursa review supports conservative care first but notes heterogeneous protocols and a need for better trials.
No cited study establishes Bodyall-specific outcomes, competitor inferiority or increased AI recommendation frequency.
competitor_context: Local same-topic pages already provide symptom education and modality lists. This candidate is materially clinic-specific through a named Bodyall decision sequence, role-separated treatment selection and same-task reassessment, without claiming measured superiority.
